content: Phenobarbital and mirtazapine both enhance sedative effects. Exercise caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while modafinil decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of modafinil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Phenobarbital and molindone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of montelukast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital and morphine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and motherwort both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and moxonidine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and nabilone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces nadolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider increasing the beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Phenobarbital and nalbuphine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of naldemedine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Avoid using naloxegol with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nateglinide by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces nebivolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider increasing the beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nefazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Neostigmine increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of neratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Nettle may enhance the sedative effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. High doses of nettle may theoretically increase CNS depression. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4; avoid use in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital and nevirapine may decrease each other's effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nicardipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nilotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of nintedanib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration, especially with P-gp inducers that are also CYP3A4 inducers, as nintedanib is a substrate of P-gp and, to a lesser extent, CYP3A4. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Nirmatrelvir, a CYP3A4 substrate, is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Significantly reduced nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. Do not initiate nirmatrelvir/ritonavir immediately after discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inducer due to the time needed for systemic clearance of the inducer. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Nirmatrelvir, a CYP3A4 substrate, is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Significantly reduced nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. Do not initiate nirmatrelvir/ritonavir immediately after discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inducer due to the time needed for systemic clearance of the inducer. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Phenobarbital and nitrous oxide both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while norepinephrine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may not be a reliable method of effective birth control during co-administration. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may not be a reliable method of effective birth control during co-administration. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone transdermal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may not be a reliable method of effective birth control during co-administration. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible due to decreased serum concentrations of norgestrel. Advise patients to use an alternative or backup method of contraception during co-administration and to continue backup contraception for 28 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. Phenobarbital and nortriptyline both enhance sedative effects. Belladonna alkaloids and nortriptyline both decrease cholinergic effects/transmission. Barbiturates may increase adverse effects, including respiratory depression, produced by toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). With therapeutic doses of TCAs, barbiturates increase metabolism and decrease blood concentrations of TCAs. Monitor closely. Belladonna alkaloids decrease olanzapine levels by pharmacodynamic antagonism and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. Phenobarbital and olanzapine both enhance sedative effects. Olanzapine increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids by pharmacodynamic synergy. Phenobarbital reduces olanzapine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
